Sibling comparison: projects/*/task.toml name/description/arena_slice for all sibling tasks; projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline/instruction.md and environment/instructions/hiring-rules.md (first ~6000 chars); projects/threadline-chat/threadline-chat/instruction.md (first ~2500 chars)
NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md line 203 ("author distinct domain behavior. Do not make nouns-swapped clones"), line 197 (reference-task domain mechanics)
evidence: Authored for this product: instruction.md is a first-person recruiting-team ask ("Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? Two things happen in it...") and hireops_rules.md is a HireOps-specific rulebook (six stages incl. Rejected 'off to the side', per-job interview places 1-50, hand-ordered cards shared by everyone, optimistic card versions with 409 + 'changed by whom', optimistic display with put-back and focus retention, all-or-none bulk move with board-order arrival, single-level undo invalidated by any later touch, staff<->candidate conversations with 30-message paging that preserves anchor, per-person unread, seen rules excluding the observer, per-user per-browser drafts surviving session expiry, candidate wording table). Seed (jobs Platform Engineer / Data Analyst / Product Designer; users, applications, messages, notes, reads, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size) and app_context.md (HireOps accounts, 120-message Noor Haddad conversation) match. All 43 functional, 5 polish and 5 visual criterion ids are task-prefixed (hro_*, hro_pol_*, hro_vis_*) and replace the template's change_me/persistence/responsive_layout placeholders; grep for sibling nouns (pellmoor, vacancy, bazaar, torquebay, threadline, CHANGE_ME) across the frozen task's .md/.toml/.json/.js found no hits. task.toml has its own name turing/hireops-recruiting-operations, distinct arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations', and a description/difficulty_explanation specific to this product. Domain-plan fit: no other sibling occupies a realtime recruiting board + candidate messaging slice. Clone check against nearest siblings: (1) pellmoor-job-pipeline is also recruiting and shares a few generic rules (no stage skipping, one-step back, one application per person per job, capacity, atomic batch). But its core is panel-assessment versioning, 1-5 scoring gates, offer/hire opening reservation, reviewed batch-offer previews with receipts, and a d3 funnel from stage history; it has no kanban order, undo, live 15-second updates, conversations, unread/seen, drafts or candidate portal. HireOps has no panels, scores, assessment versions, funnel or receipts. Different flows and different criteria, not renamed entities. (2) threadline-chat shares messaging concepts (unread, older-message loading) but is a Slack-style channel/thread/reaction product with no pipeline. Counterexample probes: an app built as a renamed Pellmoor (vacancy funnel + assessment gate + batch offers) would fail most hro_* criteria (hro_reorder, hro_undo_*, hro_live_board, hro_msg_*, hro_thread_*, hro_unread_*, hro_seen, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_*), so the rubric can't be satisfied by a sibling clone. A conforming HireOps that picks its own routes, labels or layout isn't penalised for differing from siblings, because hireops_rules.md says 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours' and app_context.md says 'never assume the reference implementation's routes, selectors or field names'. Observation (not a defect): the recruiting domain overlaps Pellmoor, and several generic pipeline rules recur. task.toml provenance says it was 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task', which I take as a user-supplied product concept; this review did not inspect that original source. This row is purely source-level. No runtime evidence is required or claimed, and no Oracle, model or portal score is implied.
